follow-up time: Variable, up to 12 days after delivery
exposure: Women who delivered by cesarean section
finding: Endometritis was the most common cause of secondary postpartum hemorrhage, and women who delivered by cesarean section were at higher risk for endometritis but lower risk for retained placental tissue compared to those who delivered vaginally.
mod_finding: Women who delivered by cesarean section were less likely to have retained placental tissue but were at higher risk for endometritis and uterine pseudoaneurysm than those who delivered vaginally.
